canonical_claim: CAS probe A (the ref-scan disagreement detector) reports each hole with the ref-log id and its direction: holes missing from the fold's own (second) scan are explainable by concurrent deletion, but holes missing from the pre-fold (first) scan are not — the object existed at the second walk and its id sits below what the first walk had already observed, so the first walk should have returned it.; Probe A detects CAS ref-prefix LIST incompleteness via two independent enumerations per GC round (the pre-fold defer scan and fold's own enumeration); it compares per-namespace id sets and reports a hole only when the id is below the OTHER enumeration's own maximum for that namespace, which excludes ordinary in-flight appends between the two walks.; Probe A compares the two existing full enumerations of `cas/refs/` instead of performing another scan, so it adds a set comparison and no backend I/O.; The chosen interim response to the LIST-hole hypothesis was mechanism-agnostic detection: compare two ref-prefix enumerations before advancing a cursor and compare intended-to-fold records with actually applied records; the permanent journal-chain fix remains required before release.; In the CAS GC-observability skipped-transaction-detector design, probe A's independence from probe B rests on the two enumerations being separate physical LIST walks; if a future optimisation merges them (listing the same prefix twice is an obvious target), probe A would silently become vacuous, and the design leaves open whether the guard against this should be a code comment forbidding the merge or a test asserting two distinct LIST walks occur.

canonical_claim: The Stage B strategic-review concentration proposal's replacement namespace-removal sequence is: (1) catalog transitions Live to Removing; (2) the fenced owner appends the terminal record; (3) GC folds the terminal record and performs one bounded cleanup pass; (4) GC writes a stable retirement marker derived only from RootNamespace; (5) GC durably publishes a fold seal with that namespace's cursor pruned; (6) GC exact-deletes `_ckpt`; (7) catalog entry deletion happens last.; Task 5 must delete a catalog entry only after the cleanup marker and cleanup-item retirement are durable, and must prune the namespace cursor before deleting the entry.

canonical_claim: Ordering the retirement marker before `_ckpt` deletion means even catalog loss cannot turn a namespace-removal window into a fresh birth; creation must check both the retirement marker and the namespace's `_ckpt` by exact key before admission and refuse if either exists; a listing omission can leak old objects but cannot make a retired namespace visible again because it is never re-admitted.

canonical_claim: Blob reachability is source-edge set membership, not a counter: one source edge is (BlobRef, source_id) where source_id = CityHash128(namespace + ref + path), with 0 reserved as the sentinel key for kCondemned rows. The edge set is idempotent under re-fold, so retries and competing attempts produce byte-identical runs. Blob in-degree is derived from a folded set of source-edge deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)` rather than stored as a mutable counter; set semantics can delay reclamation but cannot accelerate deletion.
